For the latter, the Higgs bound on the coupling differences is about two orders of magnitude below the JUNO scale, assuming a single operator valid at the Higgs mass and Standard Model production. At lower energies, we calculate pion and kaon ALP-emission rates and missing-mass spectra and compare them with PIENU and NA62 searches.

papers.title: Hidden Sector Relic Abundances from an Effective Planck Mass
papers.abstract: Hidden sectors are generic in beyond the Standard Model constructions and string compactifications. We consider models featuring hidden sectors that have dark matter candidates. The relic density is set in part by the energy-injecting inflaton branching ratio $B$ to the sector. We develop a general framework to determine the dependence on $B$ for thermalized hidden sectors by defining an effective Planck mass for the Boltzmann equations for the hidden sector degrees of freedom. We apply this framework to several representative examples, including freeze-out/freeze-in WIMPs and multi-component dark matter. We find that the fractional energy density carried by freeze-out relics (in both single and multi-component models) and monopoles produced from second order phase transitions scale as $B^{1/4}$ and thus may lead to an overclosure problem, even with $B \ll 1$. On the other hand, the energy density of freeze-in relics scales as $B^{5/4}$ and is thus cosmologically irrelevant for sufficiently small $B$. Finally, we discuss the cumulative implications of a large number of hidden sectors.

papers.title: A unified reduced-mass parametrization of effective chromoelectric interactions in hadrons
papers.abstract: We construct a unified effective mass relation in which a common reduced-mass function describes the flavor dependence of chromoelectric pair contributions, with explicit color factors connecting $q\bar q$ and $qq$ pairs. After subtracting fixed spin-weighted chromomagnetic contributions, we jointly fit fourteen spin-averaged meson and baryon masses using constituent quark masses and an additive constant shared by both sectors, obtaining a root-mean-square (RMS) residual of 4 MeV. The fitted saturating form connects the nearly saturated light-flavor contribution with increasing attraction in the heavy-flavor region. In the common saturation limit, the leading chromoelectric contribution acts as a common mass shift for each constituent and can be absorbed into effective constituent masses; the residual pair term accounts for the flavor dependence away from saturation. With the chromomagnetic interaction included, this single parameter set reproduces the ground-state meson and baryon spectra and yields predictions for multiply heavy baryons outside the calibration set. By diagonalizing the sum of the chromoelectric and chromomagnetic mass matrices, we further obtain the ground-state spectra of $cc\bar c\bar c$, $bb\bar b\bar b$, and $bc\bar b\bar c$. The fully charmed tensor mass is ${6505}{(9)(9)}$ MeV, close to recent lattice QCD results, while the upper scalar mass of {${6562}{(9)(12)}$} MeV lies in the mass region near $X(6600)$. The tetraquark masses remain relatively stable under the examined variations of the $qq$ chromomagnetic couplings. The relative $S$-wave rearrangement-decay weights obtained from color--spin recoupling can be used to identify favored decay channels under the stated spatial-overlap approximation.

papers.title: Monopole catalysis with massive fermions: the fate of the twisted sector
papers.abstract: In the massless limit a fermion scattering on the minimal $SU(5)$ monopole in the lowest partial wave produces an outgoing state with half-integer fermion number in every flavour. This state lives in a twisted sector of the Hilbert space and is now understood as an ordinary fermion attached to a topological line running back to the monopole. In the Standard Model fermion masses and confinement destroy the line at distances greater than the inverse mass scales, causing the twisted state to decay into physical asymptotic states with integer fermion numbers. We study this decay for an incoming lepton or quark of one generation. The cross-section in this partial wave saturates the unitarity bound, $σ=π/p^2$, and the energy of the outgoing state is shared among the four fermion flavours with a broad Dirichlet distribution, which sets the thresholds and the kinematics. Conservation laws allow exactly two decay channels for each incoming fermion, the helicity flip and its $(B+L)$-violating partner. For an incoming electron the $(B+L)$-violating channel is anti-nucleon synthesis, and we determine the branching ratios in two limits: the two channels are equally likely at high energy, and only the helicity flip remains at low energy, below the anti-nucleon threshold. In between we model the energy dependence. For a quark in a slow proton the $(B+L)$-violating channel is catalysed proton decay, which has no threshold and occurs with a probability close to one. Callan's statistical interpretation of the fractional state emerges in a sharper form: the state is not a superposition of two final states with equal weights, but a single state that decays into them with energy-dependent probabilities, equal only at high energy.

papers.title: Saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at LH$μ$C
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent proposal of high energy $μ^+$-hadron collider at CERN, LH$μ$C, which could be a natural extension of the LH$e$C at the end of the HL-LHC stage, we have studied expected gluon saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at DIS; these processes are sensitive to the most basic non-perturbative structure parametrizing hadronic content of small-$x$ gluons, the Weizsäcker-Williams (WW) TMD gluon distribution. For the nominal center-of-mass energy of LH$μ$C $\sqrt{s}=5.3$~TeV we have computed a large selection of observables using the ITMD framework in Mote Carlo setting, both for proton and lead target. In the context of future data-driven precise restrictions of the WW TMD gluon distribution, we have computed several azimuthal angle correlations, including the correlations between pairs of jets as well as the outgoing $μ^+$ and jet plane. We have also computed nuclear modification factors, that show a significant suppression, ranging locally between 30%-40%, depending on the observable.

papers.title: Two-loop correction to the complex-bion amplitude in a quasi-exactly solvable sextic oscillator
papers.abstract: In this study, a quasi-exactly solvable sextic potential is analyzed by two diagrammatic calculations. At positive coupling, factorization fixes the ground-state energy $E_0$ exactly and forces every perturbative coefficient to vanish. Using only Feynman diagrams, we verify this cancellation explicitly through third order. After continuation to negative coupling, the formal zero mode becomes nonnormalizable. A real instanton remains, but its one-instanton contribution to \(E_0\) vanishes. In particular, the leading shift in energy arises from a complex neutral bion. Taking an exact constrained family, we calculate its local median amplitude through two loops. The direct diagrammatic sum gives $c_{\rm 2L}^{\rm diag}=-0.750000(5)$, in excellent agreement with the exact-WKB value $-3/4$.

papers.title: Lorentz symmetry in self-supervised representation learning
papers.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) and explicit physical inductive biases have driven major advances in jet tagging, yet they are typically pursued along separate tracks. In this work, we unify both paradigms by integrating the Lorentz-equivariant Geometric Algebra Transformer slim (L-GATr-slim) architecture with the LeJEPA framework for representation learning. Pre-training on 100 million jets from the JetClass dataset, we optimize towards a latent space, which is invariant across physics-motivated jet augmentations. We demonstrate that enforcing Lorentz symmetry in the latent space is critical for representation quality and that this can be achieved either architecturally or learned via kinematic augmentations. With a standard non-invariant Transformer backbone, LeJEPA outperforms established autoregressive, masked particle modelling, and self-distillation baselines in linear- and MLP-probe accuracy, with L-GATr-slim providing further complementary gains. Across downstream benchmarks, our pre-trained models consistently outperform baselines trained from scratch or through different pre-training objectives.

papers.title: Investigating tidal heating in neutron stars via gravitational Raman scattering
papers.abstract: We present a scattering amplitude formalism to study the tidal heating effects of nonspinning neutron stars incorporating both worldline effective field theory and relativistic stellar perturbation theory. In neutron stars, tidal heating arises from fluid viscosity due to various scattering processes in the interior. It also serves as a channel for the exchange of energy and angular momentum between the neutron star and its environment. In the interior of the neutron star, we first derive two master perturbation equations that capture fluid perturbations accurate to linear order in frequency. Remarkably, these equations receive no contribution from bulk viscosity due to a peculiar adiabatic incompressibility which arises in stellar fluid for non-barotropic perturbations. In the exterior, the metric perturbations reduce to the Regge-Wheeler (RW) equation which we solve using the analytical Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi (MST) method. We compute the amplitude for gravitational waves scattering off a neutron star, also known as gravitational Raman scattering. From the amplitude, we obtain expressions for the electric quadrupolar static Love number and the leading dissipation number to all orders in compactness. We then compute the leading dissipation number for various realistic equation-of-state(s) and estimate the change in the number of gravitational wave cycles due to tidal heating during inspiral in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) band. We find that the shear-viscous contribution is small. Even for cold ($T\sim 10^5$K) and weakly compact stars it changes the number of cycles by less than $10^{-2}$, about an order of magnitude below the other conservative 4PN contributions, and it decreases as $T^{-2}$ for hotter stars.

papers.title: Prospect on constraining environment-dependent dilaton model from gravitational redshift measurements
papers.abstract: Scalar-tensor gravity represents a natural extension of general relativity. This paper investigates the prospects for constraining the environmentally dependent dilaton through atomic-clock comparisons across media of different densities. Using the scalar Compton wavelength, we assess how the finite size of the surrounding medium and screening by the clock enclosure limit the accessible region. To test the continuous-density approximation for dilute media, we model matter as a periodic lattice of spherical particles and compare an analytic Neumann solution with a three-dimensional finite-element solution on the cubic box. The continuous and discrete models give indistinguishable redshift predictions near the $10^{-20}$ and $10^{-25}$ benchmarks. In the strong-coupling regime, differences become apparent on redshift contours of order $10^{-46}$ or lower. Under the assumed environmental and instrumental conditions, comparisons involving a dense medium identify a window for probing smaller values of $A_2$, offering a gravitational-redshift test complementary to existing fifth-force searches.

papers.title: Morphological false-vacuum decay in dipolar supersolids
papers.abstract: False-vacuum decay between two morphologically distinct supersolid phases via bubble nucleation is studied in a uniform dipolar gas confined to the plane. Starting from a metastable honeycomb state, the formation of stripe phase domains is simulated numerically by means of a stochastic projected extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The speed of bubble growth is analyzed in relation to the multiple speeds of sound of the supersolid, and is found to be set by the slowest of these sounds. The vacuum decay rate is numerically extracted and compared against a minimal effective model for the Coleman bounce solution connecting the two supersolid orders. Our results establish dipolar supersolids as a novel and versatile platform for studying false-vacuum decay. This setting offers a rich structure of metastable states and collective excitations that come into play in the decay. Furthermore, here, in contrast to previous studies, bubble formation occurs directly in the real-space density and can be probed with \textit{in situ} imaging.

papers.title: Finite-density equation of state of hot QCD using the complex Langevin equation
papers.abstract: We present the results of continuum-extrapolated lattice simulations of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) above the crossover temperature and for unprecedentedly high baryon densities at the physical point, employing the complex Langevin equation. In particular, we determine the QCD equation of state by computing the baryon density as well as the pressure as functions of the baryon chemical potential and the temperature. Potential issues with wrong convergence of complex Langevin dynamics are under control and we indeed find agreement with previous lattice studies working at smaller chemical potentials, as well as with perturbative hard-thermal-loop calculations at high temperatures.

papers.title: Hadronic and partonic composition of QCD matter across the crossover
papers.abstract: We construct a phenomenological equation of state of strongly interacting matter at zero chemical potentials that provides a unified description of lattice QCD thermodynamics in terms of hadronic and partonic degrees of freedom in the temperature range $T=100$-$510$ MeV. The hadronic phase is described by the quantum van der Waals hadron resonance gas, extended by excluded-volume repulsion between mesons, while the quark-gluon plasma is modeled as an ideal gas of quarks and gluons supplemented with a phenomenological interaction term proportional to $T^3$. The two regimes are connected by a smooth crossover switching function. We determine the four model parameters - the meson hard-core radius, the strength of the partonic interaction term, and two parameters of the switching function - by fitting to lattice QCD results for the trace anomaly. In this model, hadronic contributions remain significant up to about $200$ MeV, well above the QCD chiral crossover. We also quantify the crossing contributions generated by the temperature dependence of the switching function. The switching temperature and the hadronic and partonic contributions depend on the chosen equations of state and switching function. The lattice thermodynamic data do not uniquely determine the microscopic composition of QCD matter.

papers.title: Magnetic Catalysis and Fermion Mass Generation in de Sitter Spacetime
papers.abstract: We consider the dynamics of a charged fermion in de Sitter space in the presence of a uniform background magnetic field, and discuss magnetic catalysis of chiral symmetry breaking using the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. We evaluate the mode functions of the charged fermion field in this background by imposing the Bunch--Davies vacuum condition. The gap equation is solved in the mean-field approximation. We derive analytic expressions for the gap in several limiting regimes, such as the large-magnetic-field and large-curvature limits. We find that the curvature effect restores chiral symmetry, whereas the magnetic field enhances chiral symmetry breaking through the conventional mechanism of magnetic catalysis. The phase structure associated with chiral symmetry breaking is revealed by numerical calculations.

papers.title: Levy-shaped femtoscopic sources from an exact solution of relativistic hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: An important goal of high-energy physics is to better understand the spacetime structure of particle emitting sources created in heavy-ion collisions. For a fraction of a second, a special form of matter, the so-called quark-gluon plasma (QGP), is created, which can be examined with the toolkit of femtoscopy. With the measurement of correlation functions it was determined that Lévy distributions describe the shape of hadron (pion) emission sources at freeze-out the most accurately; however, analytic solutions of hydrodynamics typically yield Gaussian sources, and power-law tails are usually attributed to the hadronic stage rather than to the fluid dynamics itself. In this article we showcase an exact solution of the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics, which aims to resolve this puzzle by providing Lévy distributions directly from hydrodynamics. A detailed analysis reveals whether the predictions of this solution are in accordance with observations; in particular, the effective temperatures from angle-averaged transverse mass distributions and the femtoscopic radii from two-particle momentum correlation functions are analyzed.
